title: Facet scene plan
description: What is on screen at every moment, why, how it moves, and whether the configured tools can make it. The director writes it with the art director to artifacts/scene_plan.json, and plan_check reads it: coverage of the narration, gaps and overlaps, variety, slideshow risk, delivery-promise fit and asset feasibility. One to three scenes for each script section; the first scene starts at 0 and the last ends at the full duration. Never three scenes of the same type in a row, and at least three types. Exact text (titles, numbers, names, calls to action, legal lines) is a text scene the composition renders, never text inside a generated image.

style_playbook.description: The style id in use (clean-professional, flat-motion-graphics, minimalist-diagram, premium-minimalist, anime-ghibli), or custom for a look designed for this piece.

type.description: The scene's render form. Templated work uses an Explainer scene type (text_card, hero_title, section_title, callout, stat_card, stat_reveal, kpi_grid, progress_bar, comparison, bar_chart, line_chart, pie_chart, terminal_scene, screenshot_scene, anime_scene, provider_chip) or a media cut (image, video). Footage, character and atelier scenes use the closest general kind: talking_head, broll, animation, character_scene, diagram, transition, generated, screen_recording.

lines.description: Ids of the script's narration lines the scene covers, in order.

script_section_id.description: The script section the scene covers.

movement.description: How the picture moves: for a still, a camera move (zoom-in, zoom-out, pan-left, pan-right, ken-burns, parallax, static); for a clip, its motion.

transition_in.description: The transition into this scene: cut, fade, slide, wipe, flip, clock-wipe or iris, from the style's set.

overlay_notes.description: Titles, captions, labels and chips over the picture, listed apart from it.

shot_language.description: Cinematography for filmed, found or generated shots.

shot_intent.description: Why the scene exists: the information it carries or the feeling it causes. A scene with no stated intent is slideshow filler.

narrative_role.description: The role the scene plays in the story.

information_role.description: What the viewer learns or feels from the scene.

hero_moment.description: True for the visual peak of the video; it holds longest and gets the most polish.

five_aspects.description: The five aspects, specified for every shot that is filmed, found or generated so prompts and searches are precise; an aspect is N/A when it does not apply, never left out. For a scene the composition renders, camera is N/A and spatial_framing describes the layout and which element holds the centre.

scene.description: Setting, point of view, time of day.

camera.description: Lens, height, angle, focus, steadiness, movement.

character_actions.description: Acting beats for rigged character animation scenes.

texture_keywords.description: Visual texture: grain, clean, anamorphic, gritty, ethereal and so on.

required_assets.description: Every asset the scene needs and where it comes from. Each must have a configured, supplied or rendered source; where a capability is unavailable, plan the alternative.

type.description: image, video, narration, music, sfx and so on.

source.description: generate: an image or video generation tool. source: stock or archive search. provided: supplied by the operator. record: a screen or camera capture. render: drawn by the composition, with no file to make.

tool.description: The tool planned to make or fetch it.

paid.description: True when the planned tool may charge, so the asset stage makes a sample first.
